Reddit has announced two upcoming changes that some long-time users may find hard to accept.

The company has already imposed one restriction on Old Reddit, and has now announced a second. Additionally, RSS support will be discontinued...

Old Reddit

Reddit made major changes to its user interface back in 2018, which drew strong backlash from users who were attached to the original layout. In response, the platform said it would continue to offer what is now called "Old Reddit" as long as users kept using it.

In August this year, that policy shifted for the first time, with the company requiring users to be logged in to access Old Reddit. The newly announced measure goes further, limiting the old interface to users who have used it within the past six months, with new users no longer able to access it.

Reddit says both adjustments are aimed at reducing corporate AI scraping of its content (though apparently, as long as you pay, that behaviour is perfectly fine).

RSS Feeds Coming to an End

The end of RSS feeds is being explained in the same way.

For subreddits that rely on RSS to handle moderation work, this change is particularly impactful. Reddit says it is aware of the situation and recommends moderators switch to Devvit apps, such as Discord Relay.

Users Are Not Happy

From the comments on the post, it is clear that many long-time users are quite unhappy with the latest developments.

What do you make of these latest changes? Share your thoughts in the comments.
